cdg.name: Paris Charles de Gaulle
cdg.label: CDG
cdg.about: Paris’s main airport. Terminal 2 is the big international side, a cluster of terminals under one long roof.

oratio.name: Hotel Oratio
oratio.label: Hotel Oratio
oratio.about: A small Left Bank hotel in the 5th, on a quiet street a few minutes from the Seine.

nord.name: Paris Gare du Nord
nord.label: Gare du Nord
nord.about: Paris’s great northern station, a vast 19th-century train shed. The Eurostar leaves from here.
nord.hours: Open from the first train until the last, early morning to late evening.

stpancras.name: London St Pancras International
stpancras.label: St Pancras
stpancras.about: London’s Gothic station, with the red-brick clock tower and the huge iron roof over the trains.
stpancras.hours: Open from the first train until the last, early morning to late evening.

royal.name: Royal National Hotel
royal.label: Royal National
royal.about: A big old hotel in Bloomsbury, a short walk from the British Museum.

lhr.name: London Heathrow
lhr.label: Heathrow
lhr.about: London’s main airport. Terminal 3 is one of the original buildings, now the long-haul terminal.

notreDame.name: Notre-Dame
notreDame.label: Notre-Dame
notreDame.about: The medieval cathedral on the island in the Seine. The towers, the rose windows, and the rebuilt spire are the sight.
notreDame.hours: Inside: Mon–Fri 07:50–19:00, Thursday until 22:00. Sat–Sun 08:15–19:30. The square outside is open all day.

ileSaintLouis.name: Île Saint-Louis
ileSaintLouis.label: Île Saint-Louis
ileSaintLouis.about: The smaller, quieter island next to Notre-Dame. One main street, and a quay you can walk the whole way around.
ileSaintLouis.hours: The streets and the quay are open all day.

berthillon.name: Berthillon
berthillon.label: Berthillon
berthillon.note: Ice cream on Île Saint-Louis. Closed Mon–Tue.
berthillon.about: The island’s famous ice-cream shop. Known for sharp fruit sorbets, not just vanilla.

duPain.name: Du Pain et des Idées
duPain.label: Du Pain et des Idées
duPain.about: A bakery famous for the pistachio-chocolate escargot, a spiral pastry, not a snail.

alexandre.name: Pont Alexandre III
alexandre.label: Alexandre III
alexandre.note: Walk the bridge on the way to the Petit Palais.
alexandre.about: The most ornate bridge in Paris. Gilded statues and lamp posts over the Seine.
alexandre.hours: The bridge is open all day.

petitPalais.name: Petit Palais
petitPalais.label: Petit Palais
petitPalais.about: A Beaux-Arts palace built for the 1900 World’s Fair. Fine art inside a spectacular building.

paulBert.name: Bistrot Paul Bert
paulBert.label: Paul Bert
paulBert.note: Steak in pepper sauce. Book. Closed Sun–Mon.
paulBert.about: A classic Paris bistro. The dish it is known for is steak in pepper sauce.
paulBert.hours: Tue–Sat, lunch 12:00–14:00 and dinner 19:30–23:00. Closed Sunday and Monday.

laRenommee.name: La Renommée
laRenommee.label: La Renommée
laRenommee.note: Filet au poivre. Book up to 30 days ahead. Dinner from 17:30.
laRenommee.about: A small restaurant on Rue Saint-Honoré. Known for a serious filet au poivre.

soane.name: Sir John Soane's Museum
soane.label: Soane's
soane.note: Free timed ticket. Closed Tuesday. Lincoln's Inn Fields.
soane.about: An architect’s house, left as a packed museum. The picture room has walls that fold open, and there is a crypt underneath.
soane.hours: Wed–Sun 10:00–17:00. Closed Monday and Tuesday. Last entry about 16:30.

tamila.name: Tamila
tamila.label: Tamila
tamila.note: South Indian on Caledonian Road. Beli 9.5. Walk from the hotel.
tamila.about: A South Indian restaurant near King’s Cross. Known for dosa and curries cooked in view of the room.

skyGarden.name: Sky Garden
skyGarden.label: Sky Garden
skyGarden.note: Free timed ticket on the Walkie Talkie. Book ahead. Bring ID.
skyGarden.about: A garden and open deck on top of the Walkie Talkie. The point is the view over the river and the City.

stJames.name: St James's Park
stJames.label: St James's Park
stJames.note: Lake, pelicans, palace view. Walk it after Buckingham.
stJames.about: The royal park between Westminster and the palace. A lake, pelicans, and the long view to Buckingham.

sainteChapelle.name: Sainte-Chapelle
sainteChapelle.label: Sainte-Chapelle
sainteChapelle.about: A royal chapel built to hold a relic of the Crown of Thorns. The upper room is almost entirely stained glass.

shakespeare.name: Shakespeare and Company
shakespeare.label: Shakespeare & Co
shakespeare.note: Left bank, next to the hotel
shakespeare.about: The famous English-language bookshop on the quay opposite Notre-Dame, with a reading room upstairs.

pantheon.name: Panthéon
pantheon.label: Panthéon
pantheon.about: The great dome of the Latin Quarter. French writers and scientists are buried in the crypt.
pantheon.hours: 1 Oct–31 Mar, 10:00–18:00. Last entry 17:15. Opens at noon on the first Monday of the month.

mouffetard.name: Rue Mouffetard Market
mouffetard.label: Mouffetard
mouffetard.about: One of the old market streets of the 5th, still lined with food shops.
mouffetard.hours: The street is open all day.

caveau.name: Caveau de la Huchette
caveau.label: Caveau
caveau.note: Jazz cellar, 5 minutes from the hotel
caveau.about: A tiny jazz cellar in the Latin Quarter, in a medieval basement. Live bands, a small floor.

louvre.name: Louvre Museum
louvre.label: Louvre
louvre.about: The royal palace turned into the world’s largest art museum. The Mona Lisa, the Winged Victory, and the Venus de Milo.
louvre.hours: 09:00–18:00 on Mon, Thu, Sat and Sun. 09:00–21:00 on Wed and Fri. Closed Tuesday. Last entry one hour before close.

orsay.name: Musée d'Orsay
orsay.label: Orsay
orsay.note: Across the river from the Louvre
orsay.about: Impressionist painting in a former railway station on the river. The clock and the great hall are part of the visit.
orsay.hours: Tue–Sun 09:30–18:00, Thursday until 21:45. Closed Monday. Last entry 17:00, or 21:00 on Thursday.

crazyHorse.name: Crazy Horse
crazyHorse.label: Crazy Horse
crazyHorse.about: Paris’s famous cabaret on Avenue George V. A tightly choreographed show of light, not a dinner theatre.
crazyHorse.hours: The show is in the evening. This night it is 20:00.

bac.name: Rue du Bac
bac.label: Rue du Bac
bac.about: A Left Bank shopping street of old shops, running south from the river.
bac.hours: The street is open all day.

grandeEpicerie.name: La Grande Épicerie de Paris
grandeEpicerie.label: Grande Épicerie
grandeEpicerie.note: Food hall on Rue de Sèvres
grandeEpicerie.about: The food hall of Le Bon Marché. One of the great grocery halls in Paris.
grandeEpicerie.hours: Open through the day and into the evening.

artModerne.name: Musée d'Art Moderne de Paris
artModerne.label: Art Moderne
artModerne.about: The city’s own modern-art museum, in a wing of the Palais de Tokyo, with a huge mural by Dufy.

trocadero.name: Trocadéro
trocadero.label: Trocadéro
trocadero.about: The terrace across the river from the Eiffel Tower. This is the classic full-length view of it.
trocadero.hours: The terrace is open all day.

eiffel.name: Eiffel Tower
eiffel.label: Eiffel Tower
eiffel.about: The iron tower built for the 1889 World’s Fair. Best known for the climb and for the lights after dark.
eiffel.hours: Every day 09:30–23:45 in late October. Last tickets about 45 minutes before close.

sacreCoeur.name: Sacré-Cœur
sacreCoeur.label: Sacré-Cœur
sacreCoeur.about: The white basilica on the top of Montmartre. The steps and the view over the whole city are the point.

tertre.name: Place du Tertre
tertre.label: Tertre
tertre.about: The painters’ square in front of Sacré-Cœur, still full of easels and portrait artists.
tertre.hours: The square is open all day.

picasso.name: Musée Picasso
picasso.label: Picasso
picasso.note: Hôtel Salé, Rue de Thorigny. Closed Monday.
picasso.about: Picasso’s own collection, hung in a grand Marais mansion, the Hôtel Salé.

rosiers.name: Rue des Rosiers
rosiers.label: Rosiers
rosiers.note: The Marais food street. Walk it, do not stop for a meal.
rosiers.about: The old Jewish food street of the Marais. Famous for falafel.
rosiers.hours: The street is open all day.

mamiche.name: Mamiche
mamiche.label: Mamiche
mamiche.note: Bakery on the way down from the hill
mamiche.about: A bakery known for a very good croissant, on the way down from Montmartre.
mamiche.hours: A bakery, open from the morning.

carnavalet.name: Carnavalet Museum
carnavalet.label: Carnavalet
carnavalet.note: Free · Paris history in the Marais
carnavalet.about: The museum of the history of Paris, in two Marais mansions. The city from Roman times to now.

falafel.name: L'As du Fallafel
falafel.label: L'As du Fallafel
falafel.about: The best-known falafel shop in Paris, on Rue des Rosiers. The queue is part of the reputation.
falafel.hours: Open from late morning until the evening.

vosges.name: Place des Vosges
vosges.label: Vosges
vosges.about: The oldest planned square in Paris. Brick arcades around a quiet garden, in the heart of the Marais.
vosges.hours: The square and the arcades are open all day.

badaboum.name: Badaboum
badaboum.label: Badaboum
badaboum.about: A nightclub in the 11th, in an old warehouse. Known for late, loud parties.

saintLazare.name: Gare Saint-Lazare
saintLazare.label: Saint-Lazare
saintLazare.about: One of Paris’s grand old stations, under a big iron roof. Trains for Normandy leave from here.
saintLazare.hours: Open from the first train until the last.

vernon.name: Vernon-Giverny station
vernon.label: Vernon
vernon.about: A small-town station on the Seine, the rail stop for Monet’s garden at Giverny.

giverny.name: Monet's House and Gardens
giverny.label: Giverny
giverny.about: Monet’s house and the garden he painted. The water-lily pond and the Japanese bridge are the famous part.
giverny.hours: 10:00–18:00, last entry 17:30. The 2026 season ends on 1 Nov.

saintMichel.name: Saint-Michel–Notre-Dame
saintMichel.label: Saint-Michel
saintMichel.about: The riverside rail station at the edge of the Latin Quarter, where the RER crosses under the Seine.
saintMichel.hours: Open from the first train until the last.

versaillesRiveGauche.name: Versailles Château Rive Gauche
versaillesRiveGauche.label: Versailles RER
versaillesRiveGauche.note: RER C terminus · 10 min walk to the palace
versaillesRiveGauche.about: The station at the gates of Versailles. The palace is a short walk up the avenue.

versailles.name: Palace of Versailles
versailles.label: Versailles
versailles.about: The palace of the French kings. The Hall of Mirrors and the state apartments are the heart of it.

versaillesGardens.name: Gardens of Versailles
versaillesGardens.label: Gardens
versaillesGardens.about: The formal gardens behind the palace. Geometric parterres, fountains, and the long Grand Canal.

garnier.name: Palais Garnier
garnier.label: Garnier
garnier.about: The old Paris opera house. A marble staircase, a gilded auditorium, and a ceiling painted by Chagall.
garnier.hours: Self-guided visit usually 10:00–17:00. A performance can close the house.

arc.name: Arc de Triomphe
arc.label: Arc de Triomphe
arc.about: The triumphal arch at the top of the Champs-Élysées, built for Napoleon’s armies. The view from the top looks down every avenue.
arc.hours: 1 Oct–31 Mar, 10:00–22:30, Tuesday from 11:00. Last entry 45 minutes before close.

zara.name: Zara
zara.label: Zara Champs
zara.about: A big high-street clothes shop, here on the Champs-Élysées itself.

britishMuseum.name: The British Museum
britishMuseum.label: British Museum
britishMuseum.about: The national museum of world history. The Rosetta Stone, the Parthenon sculptures, and the Egyptian mummies.
britishMuseum.hours: Daily 10:00–17:00, Friday until 20:30. Last entry 16:45, or 20:15 on Friday.

nationalGallery.name: The National Gallery
nationalGallery.label: National Gallery
nationalGallery.about: The national collection of European painting, on Trafalgar Square. Van Gogh, Turner, and Monet in one building.

darjeeling.name: Darjeeling Express
darjeeling.label: Darjeeling Express
darjeeling.note: 36–40 Rupert Street, Soho. Bengali. Lunch until 14:15.
darjeeling.about: A Bengali restaurant in Soho, run by an all-women kitchen. Known for home-style cooking, not a curry-house menu.
darjeeling.hours: Lunch Mon–Sat 12:00–14:15. Dinner Mon–Wed 18:00–21:00, Thu–Sat 17:00–21:00. Closed Sunday.

oma.name: OMA
oma.label: OMA
oma.note: Greek, 2–4 Bedale Street. Book. £60 if you cancel inside 24 hours.
oma.about: A Greek restaurant beside Borough Market. Known for charcoal cooking and a serious wine list.

gordons.name: Gordon's Wine Bar
gordons.label: Gordon's
gordons.about: London’s oldest wine bar, in a candlelit cellar under Villiers Street.
gordons.hours: Open from the afternoon until late.

westminster.name: Westminster Abbey
westminster.label: Westminster
westminster.about: The abbey where kings and queens are crowned. Royal tombs and Poets’ Corner.
westminster.hours: Sightseeing Mon–Fri 09:30–16:30, Saturday 09:00–16:00. Sundays are for services.

bigBen.name: Big Ben
bigBen.label: Big Ben
bigBen.about: The clock tower of the Houses of Parliament. The bell is Big Ben; the tower is the thing you see.
bigBen.hours: Parliament Square is open all day. The tower is not a walk-in visit.

dishoomKX.name: Dishoom King's Cross
dishoomKX.label: Dishoom KX
dishoomKX.about: A Bombay café at King’s Cross. Known for black daal and a room styled like an old Irani café.

leadenhall.name: Leadenhall Market
leadenhall.label: Leadenhall
leadenhall.about: A covered Victorian market in the City, with a painted iron-and-glass roof under the towers.
leadenhall.hours: Open through the weekday. Quieter at the weekend.

borough.name: Borough Market
borough.label: Borough
borough.about: London’s best-known food market, in the railway arches by London Bridge.

tower.name: Tower of London
tower.label: Tower
tower.about: The medieval fortress by the river. The Crown Jewels, the ravens, and the old walls.
tower.hours: In November, Tue–Sun 09:00–16:30, last entry 15:00. Closed Monday.

nealsYard.name: Neal's Yard
nealsYard.label: Neal's Yard
nealsYard.about: A tiny painted courtyard hidden off a lane in Covent Garden. The colours are the whole point.
nealsYard.hours: The courtyard is open all day.

fortnum.name: Fortnum & Mason
fortnum.label: Fortnum
fortnum.about: The old Piccadilly grocer, trading since 1707. The food hall is the famous part.
fortnum.hours: Open through the day and into the evening.

buckingham.name: Buckingham Palace
buckingham.label: Buckingham
buckingham.about: The King’s London palace. The façade and the Victoria Memorial in front of it.
buckingham.hours: The gates and the memorial are outside, and open all day.

hydePark.name: Hyde Park
hydePark.label: Hyde Park
hydePark.note: Carriage drive and the Serpentine. The loop is about half an hour.
hydePark.about: The great royal park in the middle of the city. The Serpentine lake and the carriage drive around it.

cluny.name: Musée de Cluny
cluny.label: Cluny
cluny.about: The museum of the Middle Ages, in a townhouse built over Roman baths. The Lady and the Unicorn tapestries are the masterpiece.

passages.name: Passage des Panoramas
passages.label: Passages
passages.about: A 19th-century covered arcade, one of the last of its kind. Glass roof, old shopfronts, near the opera.
passages.hours: The arcade is open through the day. Shops keep their own hours.

somerset.name: Somerset House
somerset.label: Somerset House
somerset.about: A palace on the Strand, built around a huge courtyard, with a terrace that opens onto the river.
somerset.hours: The courtyard and the river terrace are open through the day.

southBank.name: South Bank
southBank.label: South Bank
southBank.note: River walk by the National Theatre
southBank.about: The riverside walk on the south side of the Thames, past the National Theatre.
southBank.hours: The river path is open all day.

coalDrops.name: Coal Drops Yard
coalDrops.label: Coal Drops
coalDrops.note: King's Cross yards and the canal
coalDrops.about: Two Victorian coal warehouses at King’s Cross, turned into a brick yard over the canal.
coalDrops.hours: The yard is open all day. Shops keep their own hours.

southwark.name: Southwark Cathedral
southwark.label: Southwark
southwark.about: A medieval cathedral tucked beside Borough Market. Shakespeare’s brother is buried here.
southwark.hours: Open through the day. A service can close part of the church.

globe.name: Shakespeare's Globe
globe.label: Globe
globe.about: A rebuilt wooden Elizabethan playhouse on Bankside, as close as we have to the theatre Shakespeare used.
globe.hours: The exhibition is open through the day. A play is a separate evening ticket.

londonEye.name: London Eye
londonEye.label: London Eye
londonEye.about: The giant observation wheel on the river, opposite Parliament. The ride is a slow circle over London.
londonEye.hours: Rides run from late morning until the evening. First and last ride are on the day's board.

va.name: V&A
va.label: V&A
va.note: Next to the Natural History Museum
va.about: The museum of art and design. The cast courts, full of huge plaster copies of famous sculpture, are the showpiece.

kensingtonGardens.name: Kensington Gardens
kensingtonGardens.label: Kensington Gardens
kensingtonGardens.note: Albert Memorial, Round Pond, the Italian Gardens. The west half of the Hyde Park loop.
kensingtonGardens.about: The west half of Hyde Park. The Albert Memorial, the Round Pond, and the Italian Gardens.
kensingtonGardens.hours: Opens at 06:00 and closes at dusk.

harrods.name: Harrods
harrods.label: Harrods
harrods.note: Food halls. Knightsbridge, a short walk from the V&A.
harrods.about: The grand Knightsbridge department store. The food halls are the part worth the crowd.
harrods.hours: Open through the day and into the evening.

russellSq.name: Russell Square station
russellSq.label: Russell Square
russellSq.about: A Bloomsbury Underground station on the Piccadilly line, the one that runs straight out to Heathrow.
russellSq.hours: Open from the first Piccadilly train until the last.

luxembourg.name: Jardin du Luxembourg
luxembourg.label: Luxembourg
luxembourg.note: Formal garden south of the hotel
luxembourg.about: The formal garden of the Luxembourg Palace. Gravel paths, green chairs, and the big round basin.
luxembourg.hours: Late October, from the last Sunday, 08:00–17:15. From 1 Nov, 08:00–17:00.

tuileries.name: Jardin des Tuileries
tuileries.label: Tuileries
tuileries.note: The garden you walk out of the Louvre into
tuileries.about: The royal garden between the Louvre and Place de la Concorde. A long central path of statues and fountains.

concorde.name: Place de la Concorde
concorde.label: Concorde
concorde.about: The huge square at the end of the Tuileries. The Egyptian obelisk stands in the middle, with the Champs opening beyond it.
concorde.hours: The square is open all day.

invalides.name: Hôtel des Invalides
invalides.label: Invalides
invalides.about: A military hospital under a gold dome. Napoleon’s tomb is in the crypt beneath it.

stPauls.name: St Paul's Cathedral
stPauls.label: St Paul's
stPauls.note: Wren's dome. Book a slot if you want to climb.
stPauls.about: Wren’s cathedral, built after the Great Fire. The dome is the landmark of the City.
stPauls.hours: Sightseeing Mon–Sat 08:30–16:30, Wednesday from 10:00. Last entry about 16:00. Closed to sightseeing on Sunday.

tate.name: Tate Modern
tate.label: Tate Modern
tate.note: Free. Across the Millennium Bridge from St Paul's.
tate.about: Modern art in a former power station on Bankside. The Turbine Hall is the huge room you walk into first.
tate.hours: Sun–Thu 10:00–18:00. Fri–Sat 10:00–21:00. Last entry 30 minutes before close.

towerBridge.name: Tower Bridge
towerBridge.label: Tower Bridge
towerBridge.about: The Victorian bridge beside the Tower, with two stone towers and a high walkway between them.
towerBridge.hours: The pavement is open all day. The high walkway is extra and runs through the day.

nhm.name: Natural History Museum
nhm.label: Natural History
nhm.note: Dinosaurs. Book a free timed ticket.
nhm.about: The museum of animals, fossils, and dinosaurs. Hintze Hall is the great room with the blue whale hanging in it.

novello.name: Novello Theatre
novello.label: Novello
novello.about: A West End theatre on Aldwych, next to Somerset House. Mamma Mia! is the long-running ABBA musical here, London’s version of a Broadway show.
novello.hours: Mamma Mia! plays Monday–Saturday at 19:30. No performance on Sunday. About two and a half hours, out around 22:15.

theBridge.name: The Bridge
theBridge.label: The Bridge
theBridge.note: Halloween party under Pont Alexandre III, 22:00–05:00.
theBridge.about: A club on the right bank, under Pont Alexandre III. Saturday is their big Halloween party, dressed as a haunted manor.
theBridge.hours: This night, 22:00–05:00. Costume is welcome and not required.

hawksmoor.name: Hawksmoor Borough
hawksmoor.label: Hawksmoor
hawksmoor.note: Steakhouse beside Borough Market. Not the booked dinner. Thursday dinner is the restaurants next to the market.
hawksmoor.about: A steakhouse in a market building beside Borough Market. Known for aged beef and British seafood.
hawksmoor.hours: Monday–Thursday kitchen 12:00–15:30 and 17:00–21:30. Friday until 22:00. Saturday 12:00–22:00. Sunday 11:30–20:30.

hawksmoorKnightsbridge.name: Hawksmoor Knightsbridge
hawksmoorKnightsbridge.label: Hawksmoor
hawksmoorKnightsbridge.note: Steakhouse, 3 Yeoman's Row. Book. On Friday the kitchen closes at 22:00.
hawksmoorKnightsbridge.about: A steakhouse in a basement on Yeoman's Row, a few minutes from Harrods. Known for aged beef and British seafood.
hawksmoorKnightsbridge.hours: Friday the kitchen is 12:00–15:30 and 17:00–22:00. The room stays open until 23:00.

days.label: Overall
days.title: The whole route
days.lede: Land in Paris on 28 Oct. Numbered pins are the plan. Warm dots are restaurants, bars, and bakeries within a 15 minute walk of a stop. Pink dots are shopping streets and stores within 10 minutes, on each day, not on the overall map. Purple dots are random sights within 20 minutes, not on that day's plan. Eurostar on 3 Nov, fly out of Heathrow on 7 Nov.

events.title: Arrive CDG · CX261
events.text: Charles de Gaulle, Terminal 2A. Off the plane, immigration, bags. Consider a car with the bags, or RER B toward Saint-Michel.

events.title: Hotel Oratio, Paris
events.text: Small Left Bank hotel at 42 rue des Bernardins. This is the start and end of every Paris day.

events.title: Eurostar 9013 from Gare du Nord
events.text: Be there at 06:30, two hours before the train. Security, then passport control out of France and into the UK, both at this station. Coach 7 seat 31. Train leaves 08:32.

events.title: Arrive St Pancras
events.text: Victorian terminus on Euston Road. Walk south into Bloomsbury, or one Piccadilly stop to Russell Square.

events.title: Royal National Hotel, London
events.text: Big Bloomsbury hotel at 38–51 Bedford Way. This is the start and end of every London day.

events.title: Leave LHR · CX250
events.text: Heathrow Terminal 3. Cathay to Hong Kong, seat 59J. At check-in about 14:30, after the tube and the walk in from the station.

days.label: 28 Oct
days.title: Arrive · Montmartre · Crazy Horse
days.lede: CX261 lands 07:35. Off the plane, immigration, and bags come first. Consider a car with the bags, or the RER. The hotel is about 10:35, so the first sight is after 11:00. Breakfast was on the flight. Montmartre, lunch on the way down, then the Marais. The hotel is only a shower and a change. Crazy Horse is at 20:00. Dinner is after the show, near George V. Home about 23:15.

events.title: Arrive CDG · CX261
events.text: Terminal 2A. Off the plane, immigration, bags. Consider a car with the bags, or RER B. At the hotel about 10:35.

events.title: Hotel Oratio
events.text: Check in and drop bags. If the room is not ready, leave the bags and go. Breakfast was on the flight. Metro north to the hill.

events.title: Sacré-Cœur
events.text: White basilica on the hill. Climb the steps, Paris from the terrace, go inside if you want. The visit is shorter than a normal morning, because the flight ate the early hours.

events.title: Montmartre streets
events.text: Place du Tertre, then the lanes behind it. Artists, side streets, the walk down. Skip the bracelet sellers.

events.title: Lunch
events.text: One hour on the way down the hill, after noon. Mamiche and the other nearby pins.

events.title: Carnavalet
events.text: Free museum of Paris history in two Marais mansions. Revolution rooms, reconstructed interiors upstairs. Closed Monday, so Wednesday works.

events.title: Musée Picasso
events.text: Picasso’s own collection in a Marais mansion, five minutes from Carnavalet. One hour. Closed Monday, so Wednesday works.

events.title: Rue des Rosiers
events.text: The short food street of the Marais. Walk it. Lunch was already on the hill, so this is the street, not a second meal.

events.title: Place des Vosges
events.text: Oldest planned square in Paris. Red brick, arcades, a short sit. Cycle through the Marais to the hotel, or take the metro, and change for the show.

events.title: Hotel Oratio
events.text: Shower and change. Leave by 18:45 so you are at the door for 19:10.

events.title: Crazy Horse · 20:00
events.text: Cabaret on Avenue George V. Nude revue, tight lighting, about an hour. Doors before 20:00. Dinner is nearby, not back at the hotel.

events.title: Dinner
events.text: One hour after the show, around Alma and George V. The pins near the cabaret. Then a car or the metro home.

events.title: Hotel Oratio
events.text: Home about 23:15. Consider a car, or the metro.

days.label: 29 Oct
days.title: Islands and the 5th
days.lede: The picture day, after a night’s sleep. Notre-Dame first, because the bookshop opens at 10:00. Then Shakespeare and Company, Île Saint-Louis, and Sainte-Chapelle on the way off the island. South through Cluny, the Luxembourg, the Panthéon, and Mouffetard for dinner. The jazz cellar is on the walk home. The garden closes at 17:15 this week, and you are out before that.

events.title: Breakfast
events.text: Half an hour, then walk to the cathedral. The bookshop next door opens at 10:00.

events.title: Hotel Oratio
events.text: Out the door.

events.title: Notre-Dame
events.text: The cathedral, back after the fire. Façade, parvis, the Seine bridges. Go inside if the queue is short. You can cycle the quay the whole way around Île de la Cité. The bookshop is the doorway you just passed, and it opens at 10:00.

events.title: Shakespeare and Company
events.text: English-language bookshop on the Seine. Browse the stalls and peek at the reading room upstairs. Then east to the next island.

events.title: Île Saint-Louis
events.text: Walk rue Saint-Louis-en-l’Île, or cycle the quay the whole way around the island. Berthillon is a nearby pin, and it is open on Thursday. Lunch is here. The chapel is on the way back, along the other side of the Cité.

events.title: Lunch
events.text: One hour on the island. A nearby pin, then walk back along the quay.

events.title: Sainte-Chapelle
events.text: The west end of the island, so this is the way off it, not a separate trip. Upper chapel, the stained glass. Book a timed ticket for this hour.

events.title: Musée de Cluny
events.text: Straight off the island, on the Left Bank. The Lady and the Unicorn. Thursday it stays open until 21:00. Closed Monday.

events.title: Jardin du Luxembourg
events.text: The garden is the next walk, west from Cluny. A chair by the big basin, one lap, then on toward the Panthéon. This week it closes at 17:15, so leave on time.

events.title: Panthéon
events.text: The dome on the hill, a short walk east from the garden. Voltaire, Rousseau and Curie in the crypt. Climb the dome if it is open. Last entry is 17:15, and you are in before that. Mouffetard is downhill from here.

events.title: Rue Mouffetard
events.text: The market street down the hill from the Panthéon. Walk it, then eat here. You do not go back to the hotel for dinner.

events.title: Dinner
events.text: One hour on this street. The pins are the meal. The jazz cellar is on the walk back.

events.title: Caveau de la Huchette
events.text: On the way home through the Latin Quarter, not a new neighborhood. Doors at 21:00, music from 21:30. No reservation. One set is enough. The hotel is five minutes after.

events.title: Hotel Oratio
events.text: Home. About 22:45.

days.label: 30 Oct
days.title: Orsay · river · Eiffel
days.lede: Orsay is closed Monday, so it is today. Breakfast, the museum, lunch after noon, then Invalides and the Petit Palais. Stay for the tower lights. Dinner is there, then the metro home about 21:15. No Seine dinner, and no hotel stop before that.

events.title: Breakfast
events.text: Half an hour at the hotel, then the left bank toward Orsay.

events.title: Hotel Oratio
events.text: Leave west along the river.

events.title: Musée d'Orsay
events.text: Old railway station, now the Impressionist museum. Monet, Van Gogh, Degas.

events.title: Lunch
events.text: One hour, after noon. Nearby pins around the museum, then walk to the dome.

events.title: Hôtel des Invalides
events.text: The gold dome and Napoleon’s tomb. An hour, then the bridge.

events.title: Pont Alexandre III
events.text: Walk the bridge end to end. The gold statues and the view of the tower are the stop. The Petit Palais is on the right-bank end.

events.title: Petit Palais
events.text: Free city art museum. Permanent collection, no reservation. Closed Monday, so Friday is the day.

events.title: Trocadéro
events.text: Esplanade with the postcard Eiffel view. Photos from the terrace, then walk down through the Champ de Mars.

events.title: Eiffel Tower
events.text: Book a second-floor or summit slot. Stay for the lights. Late October is dark by about 18:30, and the tower sparkles on the hour. The blue dot is the avenues around the Champ de Mars: one lap of the lawns, not the grass. No dinner cruise.

events.title: Dinner
events.text: One hour around the tower and Trocadéro. The pins here, not the hotel. Then the metro home.

events.title: Hotel Oratio
events.text: Home about 21:15. 25 minutes on the metro.

days.label: 31 Oct
days.title: Versailles · Halloween
days.lede: The palace in the day. Crazy Horse was Wednesday. The hotel is a shower and a change, then you leave dressed. Dinner is on the right bank, by Pont Alexandre III. The Bridge is the Halloween party, under the bridge, doors at 22:00. You come home after. Giverny is tomorrow, so the morning can start late.

events.title: Breakfast
events.text: Half an hour. Coffee and something from a nearby pin, then out the door.

events.title: Hotel Oratio
events.text: Walk to Saint-Michel for the RER C west.

events.title: Saint-Michel–Notre-Dame
events.text: RER C platform toward Versailles Château Rive Gauche. Trains about every 15 minutes. Take the one that says Versailles.

events.title: Versailles Château Rive Gauche
events.text: End of the line. Walk straight up Avenue de Paris to the palace gates.

events.title: Palace of Versailles
events.text: Louis XIV’s château. Hall of Mirrors, King’s State Apartments, chapel. Passport ticket, go in as it opens.

events.title: Lunch
events.text: One hour in town, by the gates or back toward the station. The nearby pins on this map are Paris restaurants, not Versailles.

events.title: Gardens of Versailles
events.text: Le Nôtre’s parterres, Grand Canal, fountains. Walk them, or hire a bike and ride the long loop out to the canal. The blue dot on the pin is that loop. Then the RER home.

events.title: Hotel Oratio
events.text: Shower and change into what you will wear. Leave by 18:40. You do not come back until after the club. Giverny can start late.

events.title: Right bank, before the club
events.text: Metro to Invalides or Champs-Élysées Clemenceau, about 25 minutes. You walked this bridge yesterday. Tonight is the party underneath it, on the right bank. Do not go back to the hotel.

events.title: Dinner
events.text: One hour here, on the right bank. The pins by the bridge, not the 11th.

events.title: Stay out
events.text: A bar or the river until doors. You are already dressed. The hotel is for after.

events.title: The Bridge · Halloween
events.text: Club at 3 Port des Champs-Élysées, under Pont Alexandre III on the right bank. Doors at 22:00. It runs until 05:00. Costume is welcome and not required. Book a ticket. Consider a car home.

events.title: Hotel Oratio
events.text: Home. Sleep. Giverny can wait until late morning.

days.label: 1 Nov
days.title: Giverny
days.lede: Last open day of Monet’s house and gardens. Breakfast, then the TER from Saint-Lazare. Lunch is an hour at Giverny. This is the night dinner stays in the 5th: that neighborhood is the good one, and Saint-Lazare is not a dinner. Bed after. The Louvre is 09:00 tomorrow.

events.title: Breakfast
events.text: Half an hour. Later if the night ran late. Then metro to Saint-Lazare: Line 10 to Odéon, Line 4 north.

events.title: Hotel Oratio
events.text: Out the door for the train.

events.title: Gare Saint-Lazare
events.text: TER toward Rouen / Vernon-Giverny. About 50 minutes. Buy a return. Sunday trains are about hourly. Check SNCF that morning.

events.title: Vernon-Giverny station
events.text: Seasonal shuttle meets the Paris trains. About 15–20 minutes to the garden car park.

events.title: Monet’s house and gardens
events.text: Last day of the 2026 season, 10:00–18:00, last entry 17:30. Clos Normand and the pink house first.

events.title: Lunch
events.text: One hour. Les Nymphéas is opposite the garden if you want a table. Then the water-lily pond.

events.title: Gardens
events.text: The pond and a last walk. Be on a 16:20 shuttle.

events.title: Vernon-Giverny · return
events.text: Shuttle back for the Paris train.

events.title: Gare Saint-Lazare · return
events.text: Off the TER. Metro Line 4 south, then 10 to Maubert.

events.title: Hotel Oratio
events.text: Drop the day-trip bag and go straight out to eat. You are not sitting the evening here.

events.title: Dinner
events.text: One hour in the 5th. Mouffetard or a pin around the hotel. This is the exception, because this neighborhood is actually good and the station is not. Then bed. The Louvre is at 09:00.

days.label: 2 Nov
days.title: Louvre · west to the Arc
days.lede: Versailles and Orsay are closed. The Louvre is half a day, not a quick look: 09:00 until 13:00, then lunch. The walk west is shorter after that. Tuileries, Concorde, a short stop at the Arc, then Garnier before the self-guided visit ends. La Renommée is 18:00. Pack after dinner. The Eurostar is at 08:32 tomorrow.

events.title: Breakfast
events.text: Half an hour, then walk or metro to Palais Royal for the 09:00 Louvre slot.

events.title: Hotel Oratio
events.text: Out the door.

events.title: Louvre · half a day
events.text: The 09:00 timed entry, and you stay until 13:00. Mona Lisa, Winged Victory, Venus de Milo, then one more wing you actually want. Half a day is enough to see the famous rooms without pretending to finish the museum.

events.title: Lunch
events.text: One hour, after you come out. Nearby pins around the museum, or the Carrousel. Tonight’s dinner is the one that is booked, not this.

events.title: Jardin des Tuileries
events.text: Walk the central path west. Basins, statues, the chairs. This is the way out toward Concorde, not a second museum.

events.title: Place de la Concorde
events.text: Stand at the obelisk and look back through the Tuileries to the Louvre. Then walk up the Champs toward the Arc.

events.title: Arc de Triomphe
events.text: Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, from the underpass. Climb only if there is no queue. Garnier closes the self-guided visit around 17:00, so do not linger.

events.title: Palais Garnier
events.text: The opera house, and the visit to do before it closes in summer 2027. Self-guided, and it usually ends at 17:00, so this slot is the staircase, the auditorium, and the Chagall ceiling. Book online. No tickets at the door.

events.title: Passage des Panoramas
events.text: Walk the covered arcade. Glass roof, old shopfronts, a look in the windows. Not a sit-down. Dinner is a 15 minute walk south.

events.title: La Renommée · dinner
events.text: The Paris dinner to book, and the only long dinner in the city. Filet au poivre at 95 Rue Saint-Honoré. Two hours, from 18:00. The kitchen opens at 17:30, but dinner is not before 6. Reserve up to 30 days ahead. Card hold, €50 a head if you cancel inside 24 hours.

events.title: Hotel Oratio · pack
events.text: Pack. Be at Gare du Nord at 06:30 tomorrow. The ticket’s 07:32 is too tight once passport control is in the line.

days.label: 3 Nov
days.title: Paris to London · Mamma Mia!
days.lede: Eurostar into St Pancras at 10:00. Be at Gare du Nord at 06:30 so security and passport control have room. Drop bags, the British Museum, lunch after noon, then Covent Garden and Somerset House. A short turn on the river, then back to Aldwych. Mamma Mia! is 19:30 at the Novello, next to Somerset House, so this is the West End night. Dinner is there at 18:00, before the curtain. Home after the show, about 22:45.

events.title: Breakfast
events.text: Short. Bags down. Taxi to Gare du Nord, about 20 minutes.

events.title: Leave Hotel Oratio
events.text: Out by 06:10. The station block is long because of security and passport control.

events.title: Gare du Nord · Eurostar 9013
events.text: Two hours before departure. Ticket check, security, then leaving France and entering the UK, both here. Find coach 7 seat 31. Train leaves 08:32. St Pancras is just the walk out.

events.title: St Pancras
events.text: Gothic revival station. Walk south to Bedford Way.

events.title: Royal National Hotel
events.text: Check in, drop bags. 38–51 Bedford Way. The museum is ten minutes south.

events.title: British Museum
events.text: Rosetta Stone, Parthenon sculptures, mummies. Great Court and a shortlist, not the whole place. Free.

events.title: Lunch
events.text: One hour near the museum, then walk down to Covent Garden.

events.title: Neal's Yard
events.text: Step into the painted courtyard and walk the lanes around it. A short look is enough, then continue toward Somerset House.

events.title: Somerset House
events.text: Cross the courtyard to the river terrace. Go into the Courtauld for one room if you want a picture. Otherwise the building and the view are the visit.

events.title: South Bank
events.text: Cross Waterloo Bridge and walk the river path past the National Theatre. A short turn only. The show is back on Aldwych at 19:30, so you do not stay out here, and you do not walk on to the Tate.

events.title: Dinner
events.text: One hour on Aldwych or in Covent Garden, a few minutes from the theatre. Not back on the river, and not Bloomsbury. Be seated for the show by 19:15.

events.title: Mamma Mia! · Novello Theatre
events.text: The West End night. ABBA musical, Aldwych, next to Somerset House. Curtain 19:30. Book it. About two and a half hours, out around 22:15. Monday to Saturday at 19:30, no show on Sunday.

events.title: Royal National Hotel
events.text: Home about 22:45. Tube from Temple or Covent Garden.

days.label: 4 Nov
days.title: Soane · Darjeeling Express · palace
days.lede: One walk south. Soane’s, the National Gallery, Darjeeling Express for lunch, then Whitehall, the Eye, the Abbey, the park, and the palace. Dinner stays down here. You arrived at King’s Cross yesterday, so you do not go back up for Coal Drops. Hawksmoor is Friday, in Knightsbridge.

events.title: Breakfast
events.text: Half an hour, then walk south through Bloomsbury toward Lincoln’s Inn Fields.

events.title: Royal National Hotel
events.text: Out the door.

events.title: Sir John Soane's Museum
events.text: A house packed with art. See the picture room with the folding walls, then the crypt. Free timed ticket. You will not see every room, so don't try. Closed Tuesday, so today works.

events.title: National Gallery
events.text: Free. One route only: Van Gogh's Sunflowers, Turner's Fighting Temeraire, a Monet, then leave. Lunch is a 12 minute walk north, in Soho.

events.title: Darjeeling Express · lunch
events.text: Bengali home cooking, all-women kitchen, 36–40 Rupert Street. One hour, not the long London dinner. Lunch service ends at 14:15, so be seated by 12:10. Book it. Kosha mangsho if you eat meat.

events.title: Big Ben
events.text: Elizabeth Tower and Parliament. Photos from the square. The walk down from Soho is along Whitehall. The wheel is across the bridge.

events.title: London Eye
events.text: Look at the wheel from the river path. Ride it only if you already have a ticket. You are here anyway. Tomorrow does not come back.

events.title: Westminster Abbey
events.text: Coronations, royal tombs, Poets’ Corner. Back across the bridge, next door to Big Ben.

events.title: St James's Park
events.text: Lake, pelicans, the palace from the bridge. This is the walk between the Abbey and Buckingham.

events.title: Buckingham Palace
events.text: The façade and the Victoria Memorial. Guard change is mornings and not every day. This slot is the building. Dinner is near here. Do not tube up to King’s Cross. You came through St Pancras yesterday.

events.title: Dinner
events.text: One hour near the palace or the park. Not Soho, you had Darjeeling Express at lunch, and not King’s Cross.

events.title: Royal National Hotel
events.text: Home about 19:45. Tube from Victoria or Green Park.

days.label: 5 Nov
days.title: City · Bankside
days.lede: The whole east side in one line. St Paul’s, then Sky Garden and the Tower, across the bridge, Borough for lunch, the cathedral, the Globe, and the Tate. The Eye was yesterday. Dinner is back beside the market. The hall itself closes at 17:00, so this is the restaurants there, not the stalls. Hawksmoor is Friday. You do not come back here tomorrow.

events.title: Breakfast
events.text: Half an hour. Book the Sky Garden slot for about 10:45 before you leave. Bring ID.

events.title: Royal National Hotel
events.text: Tube to St Paul's. The City comes first, then you walk east, then back west along the south bank.

events.title: St Paul's Cathedral
events.text: The nave first. Climb to the Whispering Gallery and the dome only if you booked it. If not, the cathedral floor is the visit. Sky Garden is a walk east from here, so you do not save this for another day.

events.title: Sky Garden
events.text: Walk the indoor gardens, then the open deck. Photos of the river, then leave. Free timed ticket. Bring ID. The Tower is next, still east.

events.title: Tower of London
events.text: Castle, Crown Jewels, ravens, Traitors’ Gate. Book a ticket. Yeoman Warder tour if the timing works.

events.title: Tower Bridge
events.text: Walk across to the south bank. The high-level walkway is extra if you want it. Otherwise the pavement is the point. Everything after this is west along the river.

events.title: Borough Market · lunch
events.text: This is lunch, while the stalls are open. One hour under the railway. The hall closes at 17:00. Closed Monday, so Thursday works.

events.title: Southwark Cathedral
events.text: The nave, the Shakespeare memorial, and the courtyard. About twenty minutes beside the market. Clink Street is the lane on the way to the Globe.

events.title: Shakespeare's Globe
events.text: Clink Street is the bank you just walked, the old palace wall and the lane. Then the wooden theatre from the yard, or the exhibition if you go in. Keep going west. The Tate is next. The Eye was yesterday, so you stop at the Tate.

events.title: Tate Modern
events.text: The Turbine Hall first, then one floor of the free collection. You are already on this bank, so this is the visit, not tomorrow. Dinner is a 12 minute walk back east. The market hall is shut by then.

events.title: Back to the market
events.text: Walk back from the Tate. The stalls closed at 17:00. Dinner is the restaurants beside the market.

events.title: Dinner
events.text: One hour beside the market. Padella, on Southwark Street, is the walk-in pasta room. No booking. The long dinner is Friday, in Knightsbridge.

events.title: Royal National Hotel
events.text: Home about 19:30. Northern line from London Bridge.

days.label: 6 Nov
days.title: South Kensington · Hawksmoor
days.lede: Last full day, and it stays in the parks and the museums. Ride the Hyde Park loop, dinosaurs, lunch, the V&A, Kensington Gardens, then the Harrods food halls. Hawksmoor is dinner, a few minutes from the store. Home after that to pack. The flight is 17:50 tomorrow.

events.title: Breakfast
events.text: Half an hour. Book the free Natural History slot. Cycle through the parks, or take the tube to South Kensington.

events.title: Royal National Hotel
events.text: Out the door. Cycle through Bloomsbury toward the park, or take the tube if you are running late.

events.title: Hyde Park
events.text: Ride the loop. The carriage drive and the Serpentine, about half an hour. The museums are on the south edge when you finish. You are not rushing east today.

events.title: Natural History Museum
events.text: Hintze Hall and the blue whale, then the dinosaur gallery. Book the free slot. Leave the rest of the building.

events.title: Lunch
events.text: One hour after noon in South Kensington. The V&A is next door.

events.title: V&A
events.text: One wing. The cast courts, the huge plaster copies of famous sculpture, are the quick hit. Free. Kensington Gardens is the park just north.

events.title: Kensington Gardens
events.text: The Albert Memorial, the Round Pond, and the Italian Gardens. This is the west half of the park you rode this morning. You do not come back to it later.

events.title: Harrods
events.text: The food halls, not the whole store. Knightsbridge is the neighborhood you are already in. Hawksmoor is a 5 minute walk, on Yeoman's Row.

events.title: Hawksmoor · dinner
events.text: The London dinner to book, and the only long dinner in the city. Steakhouse at 3 Yeoman's Row, a few minutes from Harrods. Two hours, from 18:00. On Friday the kitchen closes at 22:00. Book online. Not Indian. Then home to pack.

events.title: Royal National Hotel · pack
events.text: Home about 20:30. Pack. CX250 is 17:50 tomorrow from Heathrow T3. Checkout is in the morning.

days.label: 7 Nov
days.title: Fly home
days.lede: Bags and checkout in the morning. Lunch near the hotel, then Russell Square. The walk over is a few minutes with bags. The Piccadilly ride is about 55 minutes, then 10 minutes from the station into Terminal 3. At check-in about 14:30. CX250 is 17:50. No dinner. That is the flight.

events.title: Breakfast
events.text: Half an hour. Then bags. Checkout is before lunch, because the airport needs the afternoon.

events.title: Bags and checkout
events.text: Finish packing, pay, and leave the bags by the door. Check-in at Terminal 3 is about 14:30, after the tube. This morning is the last hotel time.

events.title: Lunch
events.text: One hour near the hotel, bags with you. Last meal on the ground. Leave as soon as you finish. The station is a few minutes away.

events.title: Russell Square station
events.text: About 6 minutes from the hotel with bags. Piccadilly line to Heathrow Terminals 2 & 3. On this Saturday a train leaves at 13:22 and reaches the airport station at 14:18. The ride is 56 minutes. Skip a train that says via Terminal 4.

events.title: Heathrow T3 · CX250
events.text: The station is between the terminals. About 10 minutes through the subway to Terminal 3 check-in, so you are there about 14:30. Then check-in, bag drop, security, and the gate. Seat 59J, flight 17:50. Dinner is on the plane.
